findings.finding: Success envelope omits the serialized-JSON TextContent block, diverging from the Go wire on every judged success call. websearch.py:108 returns `types.CallToolResult(content=[], structured_content=output)`, with the comment (lines 105-107) claiming 'Go returns an empty &mcp.CallToolResult{}'. That is true only at the closure level: go-sdk v1.7.0's AddTool boundary (the SDK pinned by go.mod) fills Content when the handler returned nil Content with non-nil output — server.go:427-437 `if res.Content == nil { res.Content = []Content{&TextContent{Text: string(outJSON)}} }`. Every pinned success capture shows the consequence: amendments-capture.json s02/s16/s18 all have `"content_blocks": ["text"]`. The judge compares block types (harness.py norm_call:303-347 puts content_blocks in the normalized dict; judge README:107 'the list of content block TYPES is compared'; strict `old_obs != new_obs` at harness.py:1403), so the port's `content=[]` -> content_blocks [] vs ["text"] diverges s02/s16/s18 and every WebSearch success scenario. Probed the port's exact mcp 2.3.0 serialization path (runner.py:118 model_dump(by_alias, mode=json, exclude_none) -> mcp_types/methods.py:634 serialize_server_result, which only validates/sieves): content stays [] — the SDK adds no fallback. The capture was in the implementer's materials (inventory row 96 cites it). Fix is cheap and judge-safe: append a TextContent block (any JSON serialization — norm_call:344 drops the text when structuredContent exists; only the block-type list is compared). Inventory row 91 (NIL-SDK)'s 'port returns just the dict' was written for the decorator-SDK envelope; under add_request_handler the envelope is hand-built and must mirror Go's wire, per that row's own 'wire contract' clause.
findings.citation: go-sdk v1.7.0 mcp/server.go:427-437 and :954-971; migration/judge/amendments-capture.json s02/s16/s18 (content_blocks ["text"]); migration/judge/harness.py:303-347, 1403; migration/judge/README.md:107; migration/inventory.tsv row 91 (tools/websearch/websearch.go NIL-SDK); probe of mcp 2.3.0 runner.py:118 + mcp_types/methods.py:634 path (content stays [])

findings.finding: Bare generic annotations fail the §0 referee (mypy strict) while the trailer claims confidence=high. input.py:13 `INPUT_SCHEMA: dict = {` and the twin output.py:14 `OUTPUT_SCHEMA: dict = {` use unparameterized `dict`. pyproject.toml sets `[tool.mypy] strict = true`, and the strict preset enables disallow_any_generics — verified from the installed mypy 2.4.0's own flag table (main.py strict_flag list, first entry --disallow-any-generics; Makefile lint runs `uv run mypy .`). Under that flag a bare `dict` annotation is error [type-arg] 'Missing type parameters for generic type dict'. Rulebook §0: 'Every translated unit must pass make lint typecheck (ruff + mypy strict) before it counts as drafted.' Both stubs' trailers say confidence=high — the exact DEV-006 failure mode (units shipped that cannot pass the referee while trailers claim confidence). websearch.py itself annotates `dict[str, Any]` correctly; only these two stubs regress. Note the in-loop ban prevented the implementer from running mypy, so per DEV-006 precedent the trailers should have been downgraded (confidence=low) or the annotation parameterized.
findings.citation: RULEBOOK.md §0 ('must pass make lint typecheck'); §6 (trailer honesty) + deviation log DEV-006 precedent; stress-pilot pyproject.toml [tool.mypy] strict=true; Makefile lint target; mypy 2.4.0 main.py strict_flag table (probed: --disallow-any-generics first); input.py:13, output.py:14, output.py:46 & input.py:27 trailers

findings.finding: Unknown-tool error diverges from the pinned Go SDK in BOTH code and message, and the TODO's premise ('Go SDK's own message unverified') is false — the SDK source is readable. websearch.py:75 raises `MCPError(0, f"unknown tool: {params.name}")` -> JSON-RPC error code 0, message 'unknown tool: Foo'. go-sdk v1.7.0 mcp/server.go:958-961 returns `&jsonrpc.Error{Code: jsonrpc.CodeInvalidParams, Message: fmt.Sprintf("unknown tool %q", req.Params.Name)}` -> code -32602, message `unknown tool "Foo"`. go.mod pins v1.7.0 and the module source is in the cache, so the UNKNOWN rule's 'most conservative representation' was decidable from source and was decided wrong on both fields. Impact is real but unjudged (the judge only calls the two known tools, as the TODO notes) — still a wire-visible divergence from the old binary's bug-for-bug surface (§2 error-model posture: byte-exact Go output).
findings.citation: go-sdk v1.7.0 mcp/server.go:954-961; /Users/iknyazkov/Downloads/websearch/go.mod:8 (v1.7.0); RULEBOOK.md §2 error row + §2 UNKNOWN rule; websearch.py:71-75 (TODO(port) claiming 'unverified')

findings.finding: JSON null for a KNOWN argument flips Go-success into a Python error. Concrete inputs: arguments {"query":"x","limit":null} — Go's SDK unmarshals arguments via encoding/json (server.go:369-375 internaljson.Unmarshal), where null into a string/int field is a documented no-op, so Limit stays 0 -> FF-2b -> 50 -> successful search with max_results 50; the port's `input.get("limit", 0)` yields None and `None > 0` raises TypeError (websearch.py:135-136), caught by the broad except at :87 and converted to an isError result whose text is 'unsupported operand type(s) for >: NoneType and int' — a success-vs-error behavioral flip with a non-pinned message. Likewise {"query":null} yields Input(query=None) where Go yields query "". No inventory row decides null-valued known args: row 90 (SDK) accepts divergence only for UNKNOWN-arg validation, and §2's json.Unmarshal row covers non-string values (decode failure), not null. Per §5 that is an inventory gap -> flag + TODO(port); there is no TODO for it.
findings.citation: RULEBOOK.md §2 json.Unmarshal row + §5 (inventory gap -> flag it) + §2 UNKNOWN rule; migration/inventory.tsv row 90 (tools/websearch/websearch.go SDK — 'unknown-arg' scope only); encoding/json null-no-op semantics through go-sdk server.go:369-375; websearch.py:84-87, 134-139

findings.finding: The prescribed @list_tools/@call_tool mechanism does not exist in the pinned SDK — an unsatisfiable prescription the deviation log must capture at the gate. Probed mcp 2.3.0 (uv.lock): mcp.server.Server has NO list_tools/call_tool decorators (hasattr false); it exposes only add_request_handler/get_request_handler, and add_request_handler REPLACES any prior handler for the method (its own docstring), which is why the implementer chain-wraps the previous handler (websearch.py:45-79). RULEBOOK §1 mandates 'LOW-LEVEL Server ... with @list_tools/@call_tool handlers' and inventory rows 90/91/92 all prescribe 'low-level Server @call_tool handler' — none of that is literally implementable under the pin, and the sanctioned alternatives are banned (FastMCP, auto-schema). The chosen route is the only §1-compliant one and is honestly marked TODO(port) (websearch.py:38-44), but per §7 'a deviation nobody logged is a deviation nobody approved': this needs a DEV-00x entry and a §1 + rows-90/91/92 amendment queued for the human at the gate, plus the webfetch twin must adopt the same chain shape (as the TODO itself demands). Finding #1's envelope gap is a downstream consequence of the same rows being written against a decorator-SDK envelope model.
findings.citation: RULEBOOK.md §1 (MCP server row), §3 (deferred-decision markers), §7 (deviation log); migration/inventory.tsv rows 90, 91, 92 (tools/websearch/websearch.go SDK / NIL-SDK / CTX); probe of mcp 2.3.0 (no decorators; add_request_handler replace-semantics); stress-pilot uv.lock (mcp==2.3.0); websearch.py:38-44, 45-64, 100-101

findings.finding: Cosmetic: the list_tools wrapper annotates `params: types.PaginatedRequestParams | None` (websearch.py:52-54), but the SDK contract guarantees the handler 'never receives None' — absent params validate as {} against params_type (add_request_handler docstring, mcp 2.3.0 server/lowlevel/server.py; runner.py validates `{}` when params is None). adherence: STANDING QUESTION — did the implementer follow the rulebook? Mostly yes, with high fidelity on every surface the judge pins, and five deviations (2 silent, 3 documented only in-code) listed in findings. VERIFIED CLEAN, with probes: (1) TEMPLATE is byte-identical to the Go backtick literal in prompt.go (leading \n after the quote, trailing \n\t, probed equal), three %s substituted in Go's (agentName, agentName, monthYear) order, and description('Agent','Oct 2026') equals the s01 capture modulo the normalized month-year — row 89 (WIRE-TEMPLATE) satisfied. (2) INPUT_SCHEMA and OUTPUT_SCHEMA are dict-equal to the s01 capture (probed): limit NOT in required (FF-2a omitempty rationale matches fixedgo.py:37-42), exact limit property dict, results [array,null] union, FF-1 'title' key, additionalProperties false at root and items, items required [content,title,url] — rows 88/96 satisfied, including harness.py:525-549 invariants. (3) FF-2b limit semantics match fixedgo.py:43-49 exactly: 50 unless input limit > 0; 0 and negative both fall back to 50 (websearch.py:134-137); absent arguments -> {} mirrors the Go SDK's zero-Input (row 90/91). (4) month-year computed EXACTLY ONCE at registration, baked into the Tool at register() (row 93 site fact 1); datetime.now().strftime('%b %Y') is the §2 canonical mapping verbatim. (5) Inner handler is sync, no ctx, called via asyncio.to_thread (§1 async row; row 92), parameter name `input` kept verbatim with noqa per §4; typed service errors propagate unwrapped and the wrapper emits str(exc) byte-exactly in an isError text block — matching Go's SetError wire (go-sdk protocol.go:347-352), correctly grounded in the NIL-SDK row's contingency (the low-level dispatcher provably turns raising handlers into JSON-RPC errors, jsonrpc_dispatcher.py:775-779 — the implementer's source-inspection claim is TRUE). (6) Results list comprehension never emits None, title key FF-1, explicit dict construction per §2 (row 95). (7) Imports across all three reviewed files plus every sibling stub are absolute module-qualified per the manifest module map — no relative imports, no star imports, no ctx anywhere in ported signatures (async wrappers take the SDK's own ServerRequestContext, documented); all __init__.py files empty per §4; SAFETY lines on both casts per §3. (8) Trailers honest: websearch.py todos=3 (3 markers), grabber.py todos=2, grabber_test.py todos=0, all sibling stubs todos=1 — no undercounts (§6). DEVIATIONS: the five findings — (a) the success envelope's missing serialized-JSON TextContent block (silent; will fail the judge's content_blocks compare on every success scenario — the one real parity breaker in this batch); (b) bare `dict` annotations in the input/output stubs that cannot pass the §0 strict referee while their trailers claim confidence=high (silent; the DEV-006 failure mode); (c) unknown-tool code+message diverging from the readable go-sdk source under a TODO that wrongly says 'unverified'; (d) null-valued known arguments — an undecided inventory gap (§5) with a concrete success-to-error flip; (e) the §1/rows-90-91-92 '@call_tool' prescription being unsatisfiable under the pinned mcp 2.3.0 — a rulebook-level bug needing a §7 DEV entry and amendment at the gate; the in-code TODO is the correct in-loop queue marker but nobody has queued the rulebook fix.
